questions.q: What is the purpose of Lesson 15 within this chapter's arc?
options: To write a brand-new strategy document not based on earlier lessons
To replace the operating model chosen in Lesson 12
To gather everything built across Lessons 1-14 into one numbered, organized deliverables package
To conduct the final retrospective on the whole program
questions.explain: The lesson is explicitly the gathering step, pulling fourteen prior lessons' artifacts into one package before Lesson 16's synthesis writing begins.

questions.q: How are the files in the deliverables package organized?
options: Alphabetically by filename with no other structure
Grouped randomly by file size
Sorted by which domain owner's name comes first
Numbered 1 through 14 in build order, one file per lesson
questions.explain: The lesson shows a folder with files numbered 01 through 14, each corresponding to a specific earlier lesson in build order.

questions.q: What are the four checks Marcus Ibe runs across the assembled package?
options: Name consistency, CDE consistency, decision consistency, and dated-ness
Spelling, grammar, font, and page count
File size, upload date, owner initials, and color coding
Only one check: whether the folder compiles without errors
questions.explain: The lesson names these exact four checks as the consistency pass run across all fourteen files before the package is considered done.

questions.q: What specific piece of drift does the consistency check example in this lesson catch?
options: A missing SQL semicolon in Lesson 7's quality checks
Dana Whitfield's title is spelled two different ways in Lesson 1
The architecture diagram references a system that doesn't exist
DateOfBirth appears in Lesson 6's classification but is missing from Lesson 3's CDE register
questions.explain: The lesson uses this specific example — DateOfBirth appearing in classification but missing from the CDE register — to show what the CDE consistency check is designed to catch.

questions.q: Why does this lesson frame assembling the package as governance work rather than clerical work?
options: Because copying files is technically difficult
Because only executives are allowed to copy files
Because a package with silent inconsistencies between its own documents looks finished when it isn't, which is worse than an honest, visible gap
Because it requires a specialized file format
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly argues that undetected inconsistency is more dangerous than an acknowledged gap, making the consistency check itself a governance activity, not mere clerical assembly.
